replication.target_description: Initial-phase standardised piecewise latent growth-curve slope for self-efficacy in type 2 diabetes patients receiving the intervention; initial intercept and slope constrained equal across subsequent how/why booster conditions. Known mismatch: the assigned description specifies participants versus a control group, but no untreated control group was included in the initial phase.

n.sample_role: Participants retained in the psychological/behavioural piecewise LGCM analyses; initial-phase common slope, with all available repeated assessments incorporated. Not an untreated-control comparison.
n.exclusions: From 160 recruited: four with only one nonbaseline questionnaire, fourteen with no questionnaires, and one who attended no group sessions were excluded. Baseline-only respondents and 13 with no baseline but at least two later questionnaires were retained.

notes: Only the replication side was assigned. The supplied reference title and DOI match the primary source. Outcome names and the p.10 primary-outcomes section/Table 1 identify the initial-phase results; no mapping by row order or numeric agreement was used. Second, the initial phase of our study did not include a control condition. The printed initial-phase slope is recorded as the actual located result, with target_match=false for the absent control comparison; it must not be treated as an intervention-versus-control coefficient. Table 1 explicitly identifies standardised estimates. The 141 is the explicitly retained analysis sample, not recruitment N=160; LGCM incorporates all available data (p.116/PDF p.9). Baseline/T2/T3/T4 questionnaire counts are 128/98/80/93 and are not summed. No N arithmetic or coefficient conversion was performed. Other Table 1 phase-specific candidates (not substitutes for the initial effect): booster how −.17, why −.10; follow-up how −.35, why −.21. Initial slope 90% C.C.I. .04; .59. Model-fit PPP .24 is not a slope-test p-value. The p’s < .001 in the nearby text concern correlations between the two psychological measures, not either slope, and were not extracted as target p-values. Authors’ successful verdict concerns initial improvements and their maintenance, not a controlled contrast or added booster effectiveness. PDF pp.6 and 10 were rendered and visually inspected.
